title.narrative: ILO Economic Empowerment in Transport Corridors 2011-2014

description.narrative: ILO's project aims at preventing new HIV-infections in transport corridors through six SADC-countries, Southern Africa, with focus on women and men working in the informal sector. Specific focus will be to strengthen women's economic situation. Policy makers and promoters shall be able to make evidence based decisions to mainstream the economic empowermentmodel into HIV regional and national agendas

ILO-projektet syftar till att minska spridningen av HIV/AIDS i södra Afrikas transportkorridorer, främst bland kvinnor och män som arbetar inom den informella sektorn. Särskild betoning ligger på att stärka kvinnors ekonomiska situation. Programmet skall genomföras i 6 SADC-länder. Programmet är en fortsättning av tidigare Sidastött projekt.

General question: Results related to the intended outcome 2016Question: Summarise results related to the intended outcome (this information will be sent to Open Aid)Answer: The programme managed by ILO ended in July 2016 and has, based on an independent evaluation reported progress against targets in terms of building business development skills which has led to increased economic empowerment among women. ILO has also reported progress towards policy and advocacy efforts with governments to integrate gender and HIV/AIDS into economic policy frameworks. This has also led to several established collaborations with companies from the private sector, among them the Cavmont Bank in Zambia and EcoNet Wireless in Zimbabwe. Advocacy efforts led to governments' support and in South Africa a para-governmental organization called Small Enterprise Finance Agency made $1 million available for beneficiaries within the programme. An estimated $3,1 million additional funds were invested in the programme due to established collaborations and platforms generated by ILO.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
